findings.reason: §4 must state that it populates `description_supplements`/`point_flux_loops`/`polygon_sections` (and name the evidence each carries) rather than leave open that it will add a parallel static-description slot.
findings.text: §4 proposes a "range-scoped machine map" carrying static per-phase description values (conductor elements, loop and probe positions, vessel filaments) and says "any schema slot this needs names ... a source that is static over a map's shot range", but the schema already has `DescriptionSupplement` ("Static machine-description values selected by the same shot range"), `PointFluxLoopDeclaration` (a static loop position absent from pulse arrays) and `PolygonSectionDeclaration`/`StructureAssembly` (shaped conductor sections assembled into repeated DD structures), all populated by `mast.json` (21 uses of these keys, blocks at lines 3503 and 32319) — so the section is describing the intent of a slot that already exists and is exercised, not a slot it must add

findings.reason: §6 should record each JT-60SA verdict as a `FluxLoopPositionDeclaration` (undecided ones included) so the JT-60SA map reuses the MAST mechanism and the reader stays machine-agnostic, rather than leaving the verdict's storage unstated.
findings.text: §6's per-channel vacuum adjudication ("fixes ... the loop sign, the probe sensitive axis, the unit factor and whether the declared position is consistent") reproduces, as a method, the `FluxLoopPositionDeclaration` slot the schema already carries — "one vacuum-measurement verdict for an acquisition address over an inclusive shot range", with the `FluxLoopPositionVerdict` enum (`nominal-table`/`reconstruction`/`undecided`) and `Catalog.flux_loop_positions_for(shot)`, and §6 itself invokes "the adjudication that settled MAST's nineteen disputed loop positions" — yet the plan never names this slot as where JT-60SA verdicts are recorded

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the three new surfaces are each small over substantial behaviour (one batch-fetch function plus one cache writer over ssh/batching/serialization; one exporter function over unit/sign/COCOS collapse; one remote script for the EQDB record), and the design extends deep owners (`transform_engine.py`, `artifact_resolution.py`, `geometry_adapter.py`) rather than spreading new wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan names its owners and extends them: `imas_ambix/data/paths.py` (`JT60SA_ROOT` beside `MIRROR_ROOT`), `imas_ambix/data/manifest.py`/`cli.py` (the bulk path it deliberately does not take), and `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py` `resolve_machine_description` ("gains a machine to resolve", not a second resolver); its one chosen fork is justified and has no ambix owner to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; each section that introduces public surface states in its own text why nothing is retired (§2 "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §3 "retires nothing, because ambix has no remote reader today"; §7 "retires nothing, because no equilibrium-database reader exists in ambix"), and §4's static-description need is met by the existing `DescriptionSupplement` slot rather than a new family member.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched codex (`enumerate_edas.py`, `executor.py`, `ssh_worker.py`, `serialization.py`) and ambix's engines, but did not search the machine-map schema's own static-description slots, which are live in `imas_ambix/data/machine_maps/schema.yaml` and populated by `mast.json`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one place the design could be a thin layer over existing machinery, the EDDB extractor over imas-codex's remote layer, states why that layer cannot be reused (it would make codex's graph, LLM and tool-installation dependencies a dependency of every ambix read) and ambix genuinely owns no remote reader today (verified: no ssh-run helper anywhere under `imas_ambix/`; the only `subprocess` uses are `s5cmd` S3 copies and `sbatch`).
